chunks: Nothing is said to you which had not been said to other apostles before you. Surely your Lord is the lord of forgiveness, but also the lord of severe retribution.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the consistency of the message given to all prophets?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis to validate the continuity of prophethood (Tawatur), reassures the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) that the accusations leveled against him mirror those faced by earlier messengers, thereby establishing a shared prophetic legacy. It underscores the divine balance of mercy and justice, reminding the community that while God is All-Forgiving, His retribution is severe for those who reject the truth, a theme central to Shia theological discussions on the inevitability of divine accountability.
